newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: FIVE FIRMS QUALIFY IN GUATEMALA TELEPHONE SALE.
newsitem.headline: FIVE FIRMS QUALIFY IN GUATEMALA TELEPHONE SALE.

text.p: Five companies will bid for a stake in state-owned Guatemalan Telephone Company (Guatel) when it is sold to the private sector, officials said on Monday.
"We have pre-qualified five of the most important operators in the world of telecommunications," Guatel Manager Alfredo Guzman told reporters at a news conference.
France Telecom, GTE Corp, MCI Communications Corp, SBC Communications Inc, and Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex) will compete for the sale through their international subsidiaries, Guzman said.
The five companies were the only ones that presented pre-qualifying papers to J.P. Morgan Securities, which is advising the Guatemalan government on the sale.
On August 18 the pre-qualifiers will visit Guatel to do research before the bidding phase. Guzman said the sale should be completed by October.
The government will not set a minimum price for Guatel but will reserve the right not to sell if none of the bids are acceptable, Guzman said.
Some experts say the phone company, which operates only 350,000 phone lines in this country of 10 million people, may be worth approximately $700 million.
The government aims to raise hundreds of millions of dollars, improve service and build up the telephone network with the sale of Guatel.

The buyer will have the option to acquire a stake of between 51 percent and 95 percent in the company. The shares are currently being held in a trust, and after the sale is complete they will be sold out of the trust to the buyer.
The remaining five percent of the shares will be offered to Guatel employees, Guzman said.
